issues.description: The problem statement specifies make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None (i.e., the function must accept a depolarization probability p), but the template's make_y_state in msd.py is declared without the p parameter. The solution implements make_y_state(circ, q, p). This parameter mismatch is structural: students following the problem will implement or call make_y_state with three arguments, but the template signature will cause confusion or immediate TypeError if they try to run or adapt the provided template code.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template declaration of make_y_state to include the depolarization parameter p, matching the problem specification and the solution: def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None. Update the template docstring to document the p parameter and the expected noise behavior so students have a consistent signature to implement against.

issues.description: The make_y_state function's signature is inconsistent between the problem statement / expected API and the template: the problem statement (and the solution) specify make_y_state(circ, q, p: float) including a depolarization parameter p, but the template stub declares make_y_state(circ, q) without the p parameter. This mismatch can confuse students about the required function signature and how to pass the noise parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template function signature to match the problem statement and solution by adding the depolarization parameter p: def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None. Also ensure the template docstring mentions the p parameter consistently.
